native_ownership.responsibility: Refactor existing backend code in .NET, ASP.NET Core, Node.js, Bun, NestJS, Elysia, TypeScript, or JavaScript applications
excludes: Adding new backend behavior is owned by backend-implement or its language/framework specialization
Read-only backend correctness and risk assessment is owned by backend-review

risk.rationale: The skill changes repository structure while preserving characterized API, persistence, authorization, job, provider, error, and observability behavior.

positive.prompt: Refactor an existing backend only after characterizing API, persistence, auth, job, provider, error, retry, observability and performance behavior; preserve repository pins and public contracts.

Remove hidden coupling and duplicate I/O without changing authorization, transaction, ordering, cancellation, idempotency or provider-effect behavior and without migrating language/framework/ORM/test stack.

negative.prompt: Implement an already-specified generic backend endpoint and its persistence behavior, including validation and focused tests; there is no defect, refactor, or framework-specific requirement.
Review backend code and return findings only without changing repository files.

scenarios.prompt: Refactor a side-effectful backend handler with weak tests. The proposal adds TypeScript/Zod, changes ORM and async model, parallelizes calls and extracts layers while public errors, authorization, transactions and retries are not characterized.

assertions.criterion: Keeps the answer within backend-refactor's stated responsibility and does not recreate native Codex orchestration.

Uses the supplied fixture as authoritative repository context, may re-check that evidence during execution, and does not invent file contents, package-manager commands, or exact paths that the fixture does not provide.
Uses an ordered, risk-driven workflow rather than a static checklist and does not bypass material missing evidence, incompatible capability, failed validation, or unsafe authority.

Characterizes caller-visible and persisted/effect behavior first, preserves API/errors/auth/transactions/idempotency/order/cancellation/telemetry, makes the smallest structural change, and rejects incidental language/framework/validator/ORM/async/test migrations or unproven parallelization.

Names the fixture-provided focused test, affected test, type-check, and build categories, states exact command names come from the manifest and none ran, and makes completion depend on the required checks without inventing a package manager.

Reports enough hypothetical repository context to ground the decisions or proposed changes, not-yet-executed checks and expected acceptance evidence, residual risks, and unresolved external boundaries without inventing results.
Keeps optional provider or version detail subordinate and loads a linked reference only when needed; does not expand into a neighboring skill's primary ownership.

scenarios.prompt: Refactor a payment workflow whose timeout, duplicate delivery, tenant authorization and transaction rollback behavior are ambiguous. Preserve behavior and explain proof before restructuring.

assertions.criterion: Before any material mutation, resolves applicable exact targets, authority or permissions, ownership, and recovery or rollback. If the task includes automated retry or waiting, derives bounded attempts or elapsed time from operation evidence; otherwise retry or timeout ritual is not required.
Rejects uncharacterized behavior, stack migration, client validation as authorization, timeout-means-failure, speculative abstractions and parallel I/O without proven independence.
Compares before/after API and persisted/effect outcomes for wrong tenant, duplicate/concurrent invocation, conflict, timeout-after-effect and rollback; typecheck or unit mocks alone are not proof.
Does not invent a framework version or version-gated API when the task provides no release context.

scenarios.prompt: Use backend-refactor in an existing project whose manifests and lockfiles pin an older supported release. A newer stable release also exists. Choose compatible guidance without silently upgrading.

assertions.criterion: Uses installed manifests, lockfiles, runtime files and capability evidence for an existing project; treats an upgrade as a separate migration.

Checks the cross-stack compatibility dimensions applicable to the selected repository, such as engine, peers, compiler/framework, test runner, or deployment runtime, without demanding irrelevant dimensions.
Verifies a selected command or API with at least one applicable capability source such as installed/generated types, CLI help, configuration schema, or matching official documentation.

scenarios.prompt: Start a greenfield project that needs backend-refactor. No manifest or lockfile exists yet. Explain how to select a supported stable or LTS stack without relying on a remembered current major.

assertions.criterion: Resolves stable or LTS release data at execution time from the configured official sources, checks cross-stack compatibility, and lets the generated manifest and lockfile become authority.
